;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2018 Gaza border protests]]
**[[Israel]]i Defence Minister [[Avigdor Liberman]] says the nation will maintain its tactics at the [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]]n border of shooting anybody who approaches the fence, and calls on [[Hamas]] to cease hostilities in exchange for aid. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liberman-says-idf-will-not-change-open-fire-policy-on-gaza-border/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
**[[Human Rights Watch]] claims there was no evidence of any threat to [[Israeli Defence Forces|Israeli soldiers]] and calls the killings 'unlawful' and 'calculated'. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2018/04/killing-palestinians-gaza-unlawful-calculated-180403060222559.html (''Al Jazeera'')]
**The death toll rises to eighteen. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/middle_east/palestinian-dies-of-wounds-bringing-gaza-death-toll-to-18/2018/04/02/d6e467f0-3653-11e8-af3c-2123715f78df_story.html?utm_term=.f017bf19913d (''The Washington Post'')]
**[[Hamas]] claims Israeli forces fatally shoot a 25-year-old man at the border fence near [[Bureij]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/palestinians-say-man-shot-dead-by-israeli-troops-on-gaza-border/ (''The Times of Israel'')] 
*[[Yemeni Crisis (2011–present)]]
**The [[Saudi Arabia|Saudi]]-led Arab Coalition says the Saudi Arabian Navy repelled an attack by [[Iran]] and [[Houthi]]s against a Saudi-flagged oil tanker in the [[Red Sea]]. [http://www.arabnews.com/node/1278466/saudi-arabia (''Arab News'')]
*[[Poisoning of Sergei and Yulia Skripal]]
**Military scientists at [[Porton Down]] state they are uncertain of the source of the [[nerve agent]] used, but are "completely confident" it was a [[Novichok]] agent. [http://www.itv.com/news/2018-04-03/defence-experts-unsure-of-source-behind-novichok-spy-attack-salisbury/ (ITV)]
**[[Russia]] requests for the [[United Kingdom]] to release "every possible element of evidence" proving Russian involvement and requests the Executive Council of the [[Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons]] to call a [[special session]] tomorrow. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/salisbury-attack-russia-west-war-trigger-spy-poisoning-nerve-agent-general-evgeny-buzhinsky-a8286351.html (''The Independent'')]
*Eyewitnesses and officials say an [[Afghanistan|Afghan]] airstrike targeted a [[madrasa]] being used as a meeting place by the [[Taliban]] in [[Kunduz]] during a graduation ceremony, with casualties including civilians. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2018/04/180402182156971.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Terrorism in Pakistan]]
**The [[United States]] designates the [[Milli Muslim League]] and [[Tehreek-e-Azaadi Jammu and Kashmir]], both [[Pakistan]]i groups, as terrorist organisations. [https://www.rferl.org/a/u-s-milli-muslim-league-u-s-terror-list/29141811.html (Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty)]
**Pakistani Interior Minister [[Ahsan Iqbal]] says the government will contest a court ruling allowing MML's participation in upcoming elections this year. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-04-03/pakistan-to-contest-alleged-terror-group-entering-politics-jfjepmhq (Bloomberg)]
**[[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] claims responsibility for the deaths of four [[Christianity|Christians]] in [[Quetta]], [[Pakistan]] on April 2nd. [https://www.ucanews.com/news/four-catholics-killed-in-pakistan-terrorist-attack/81957 (UCA News)]
*[[Terrorism in the United Kingdom]]
**[[West Yorkshire Police|Police]] raid two homes in [[West Yorkshire]] and detain two men suspected of "being concerned in the commission, preparation or instigation of acts of terrorism". [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/crime/terror-plot-west-yorkshire-two-men-arrested-police-latest-updates-dewsbury-counter-terrorism-north-a8286206.html (''The Independent'')]
**The [[Police Service of Northern Ireland]] says it was firebombed at a march in [[Londonderry]] to commemorate a [[the Troubles|Troubles]] attack, calling the assaults an "attempt to kill or maim" officers. [https://www.newsletter.co.uk/news/crime/petrol-bomb-attacks-attempt-to-kill-psni-officers-1-8442063 (''News Letter'')]
**Police launch an investigation after Robert McClenaghan, a convicted ex-[[Irish Republican Army]] bomber, claims online to have planted a large number of bombs during the Troubles. [https://www.newsletter.co.uk/news/psni-to-probe-claims-of-ex-ira-bomber-on-victims-forum-1-8441932 (''News Letter'')]
*[[Terrorism in Indonesia]]
**Failed suicide bomber Kurnia Widodo tells a court in [[Jakarta]] he believes imprisoned cleric Aman Abdurrahman is [[ISIL]]'s [[Indonesia]]n leader. [https://www.theaustralian.com.au/news/world/bombmaker-names-aman-abdurrahman-as-isis-leader-in-indonesia/news-story/18d3cb98e47e01c5ae7053405656b566 (''The Australian'')]
*[[Terrorism in Italy]]
**[[Italy|Italian]] authorities say a major terror alert in [[Rome]] last week was for an innocent man whose fiancé had made false, anonymous accusations to the Italian embassy in [[Tunisia]]. [http://english.alarabiya.net/en/variety/2018/04/03/Woman-fabricates-terror-claims-on-Tunisian-fianc-causes-Rome-emergency-alert.html (Al Arabiya)]

;Arts and culture
*[[Censorship in the United Kingdom]], [[Legal status of pornography]]
**The [[British Board of Film Classification]] issues draft guidelines outlining how it plans to enforce planned blocks on online [[pornography]] unless it comes with [[age verification]] systems. The blocks were initially planned to come into force this month. [https://www.wired.co.uk/article/bbfc-porn-consultation-age-verification (''Wired'')]

;Business and economy
*Following the bankruptcy of [[United Kingdom|UK]] engineering outsourcing firm [[Carillion]], the Official Receiver reveals more than half of the roughly 20,000 employees have found new jobs. [https://news.sky.com/story/more-than-half-of-carillion-workers-find-new-jobs-after-firms-collapse-11315162 (Sky News)]
*[[United Kingdom|UK]] retailer Conviviality, owner of [[Bargain Booze]], says it intends to appoint administrators within ten days. [http://citywire.co.uk/wealth-manager/news/fund-managers-stung-as-conviviality-nears-collapse/a1106911 (Citywire)]

;Disasters and accidents
*A bus crashes in rain and poor visibility at the [[Mporokoso]]-Luwingu junction in [[Zambia]], killing four and injuring 41. [https://www.daily-mail.co.zm/4-die-in-bus-crash/ (''Zambia Daily Mail'')]
*A double-decker sightseeing bus collides with a car in [[Hamburg]], [[Germany]], leaving eleven injured. [https://www.thelocal.de/20180403/crash-involving-sightseeing-bus-in-hamburg-leaves-four-badly-injured (''The Local'')]
*The [[Prisons and Probation Ombudsman]] launches an investigation after a burglar dies from burns suffered in a fire in his cell at [[HMP Risley]] in [[England]]. [https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/hmp-risley-prisoner-dies-fire-14486055 (''Manchester Evening News'')]
*A report into the partial collapse of an [[Edinburgh]] school reveals similar construction errors in nineteen other public buildings in the city. [http://www.constructionenquirer.com/2018/04/03/more-buildings-hit-by-scottish-school-collapse-defects/ (''Construction Enquirer'')]
*An [[air traffic control]] system failure in [[Europe]] delays up to 15,000 flights, according to the [[European Organisation for the Safety of Air Navigation]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-43633094 (BBC)]
*Four people, all British nationals, are killed in a head-on collision with a pick-up truck in the U.S. state of [[Florida]], according to [[Titusville Police Department]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-bristol-43634901 (BBC)]
*Two underground trains collide in [[Duisburg]], [[Germany]], injuring at least 35. [http://www.euronews.com/2018/04/03/dozens-injured-in-underground-train-collision-in-duisburg (Euronews)]
*At a [[United Nations]] donor conference nations pledge [[United States dollar|US$]]2 billion in aid for [[Yemen]], with almost half coming from [[Saudi Arabia]] and the [[United Arab Emirates]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2018/apr/03/saudi-arabia-united-arab-emirates-pledge-nearly-1bn-aid-yemen-un-conference (''The Guardian'')]
*A CH-53E Super Stallion helicopter carrying [[US Marines]] crashes near [[El Centro]], [[California]] killing four people. [https://www.militarytimes.com/news/your-military/2018/04/04/ch-53-crash-kills-four-crew/ (Military Times)]
*A bus carrying US tourists crashes near [[Los Ramones]], [[Mexico]]. One person dies and at least 20 are injured. [http://www.wfaa.com/article/news/1-dead-20-injured-when-bus-from-houston-crashes-in-mexico/285-534617703 (WFAA)]
*A 13-year-old boy is rescued after falling into a sewer and becoming trapped for 12 hours in [[Los Angeles]]. [https://iwradio.co.uk/2018/04/03/boy-rescued-after-12-hours-trapped-in-los-angeles-sewer/ (Isle of Wight Radio)]
*A military pilot is killed when his [[Chengdu J-7|F-7]] [[fighter jet]] crashes into a paddy field in [[Kyunkon|Kyunkone]], central [[Myanmar]]. [http://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/pilot-dies-in-myanmar-military-plane-crash (The Straits Times)]
*A fire in a [[Bangkok]] apartment building kills three and injures 60. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/news/general/1439910/rajtevee-apartment-fire-kills-3?utm_source=bangkopost.com&utm_medium=article_news&utm_campaign=most_view_bottom_box (The Bangkok Post)]

;Health and environment
*The [[Worldwide Fund for Nature|WWF]] describes [[Germany]]'s rivers as being in a state "bordering on critical" after it emerges more than 90% do not meet [[European Union]] standards for cleanliness and ecological quality. [https://www.thelocal.de/20180403/90-per-cent-of-germanys-rivers-below-eu-environmental-standards (''The Local'')]

;International relations
*[[Latvia–Russia relations]]
**[[Russia]]n [[Parliament of Russia|MPs]] call for sanctions against [[Latvia]] in response to plans to make [[Latvian language|Latvian]] mandatory for all students in [[education in Latvia|secondary schools]] in the country, which is a quarter ethnic Russians. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-43626368 (BBC)]
*[[Egypt–Saudi Arabia relations]]
**[[Saudi Arabia]] lifts a ban on imports of frozen [[guava]] from [[Egypt]]. [https://www.egypttoday.com/Article/3/46916/Saudi-Arabia-lifts-ban-on-Egyptian-frozen-guava (Egypt Today)]
*Member states of the [[Nile Basin Initiative]] hold their annual meeting in [[Khartoum]] after a two-year hiatus. [https://aa.com.tr/en/africa/nile-basin-states-talk-water-sharing-in-egypt-s-absence/1107062 (Anadolu Agency)]
*The [[United Nations]] places sanctions on a [[North Korea]]n ship for conducting fuel transfers in breach of UN sanctions. [https://www.pmnewsnigeria.com/2018/04/03/north-korean-ship-sanctioned-for-fuel-transfer-at-sea/ (P.M. News)]
*[[Gulf Cooperation Council]], [[Qatar–United States relations]]
**[[Reuters]] reports the [[United States]]' planned meeting this spring with [[Arab states of the Persian Gulf|Gulf Arab]] leaders is postponed because of the ongoing dispute between [[Qatar]] and other U.S. allies in the [[Middle East]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-gulf-summit/white-house-postpones-planned-trump-summit-with-gulf-leaders-sources-idUSKCN1HA2H2 (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*[[2017 Saint Petersburg Metro bombing]]
**On the first anniversary of the attack [[Russia]]'s Investigative Committee releases a statement saying they have identified all participants, have eleven suspects in custody, and have almost concluded their investigation. [https://themoscowtimes.com/news/11-terror-suspects-custody-one-year-after-st-petersburg-metro-bombing-61027 (''The Moscow Times'')]
*Police say a firebombing of a bus in [[Driekop]], [[South Africa]], killed six people. [https://www.iol.co.za/news/south-africa/limpopo/6-killed-after-petrol-bomb-thrown-at-bus-in-limpopo-14213045 (Independent Online)]
*A court in [[Kuwait]] sentences a [[Lebanon|Lebanese]] man and his [[Syria]]n wife to death [[trial in absentia|''in absentia'']] for the murder of their [[the Philippines|Filipino]] maid. The case sparked an [[Interpol]] manhunt and diplomatic tensions. [https://edition.cnn.com/2018/04/03/middleeast/kuwait-philippines-maid-murder-sentence-intl/index.html (CNN)] [http://www.news.com.au/finance/work/pair-sentenced-to-death-following-discovery-of-womans-body-in-freezer/news-story/1fbf63b9d5c00f265a149b362b0ed0fc (News.co.au)]
*Three men plead not guilty to [[arson]] and [[manslaughter]] in connection to the deaths of five people in an explosion at a shop in [[Leicester]], [[England]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-leicestershire-43626614 (BBC)]
*[[YouTube headquarters shooting]]
**A shooting at [[YouTube]] headquarters wounds four. The gunwoman takes her own life. [https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2018/apr/03/youtube-headquarters-report-shooting-police-san-bruno (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Germany|German]] police defuse a parcel bomb in [[Berlin]]. It is thought to be the fourth device sent by a blackmailer targetting [[DHL]]. [https://www.thelocal.de/20180404/police-say-dhl-blackmailer-has-struck-again-after-parcel-bomb-found-in-berlin (''The Local'')]
*The editor of ''Citylife Chiang Mai'' apologises to [[Chiang Mai]]'s governor after being threatened with criminal charges for sharing on [[Facebook]] a painting by a student that depicted historic kings in anti-pollution masks. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/news/general/1439958/facing-jail-editor-apologises-for-anti-pollution-posting?utm_source=bangkopost.com&utm_medium=article_news&utm_campaign=most_view_bottom_box (''The Bangkok Post'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2017–18 Spanish constitutional crisis]]
**[[Germany|German]] prosecutor requests permission to extradite [[Carles Puigdemont]] to [[Spain]]. Puigdemont is in preventive detention in Germany since his March 25 arrest under a [[European Arrest Warrant]] on the grounds of risk of absconcion. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/apr/03/german-prosecutors-ask-court-to-permit-carles-puigdemont-extradition-to-spain (''The Guardian'')]
